speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe your gait and limb ataxia in more detail, and tell me about your significant medical history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the ataxia appears to be asymmetric, affecting the right side more significantly. When did these symptoms first begin, and have they progressed rapidly over days or slowly over months?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, I am concerned about the risk of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Have you experienced any cognitive changes, such as memory loss or confusion, or any visual disturbances like blurred vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to rule out other causes like B12 deficiency, which can also occur in Crohn's patients. Do you experience any numbness, tingling, or a "pins and needles" sensation in your hands or feet?
